# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Thinking: My hands tell me only this much: there is a large button, embossed so I can read it by touch — it says PUSH TO DEFUSE — and exactly three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. The display and the light give my fingers nothing; whatever they show exists only for the Deaf one's eyes, and the wire colours likewise. The embossed label is exactly the kind of thing a bomb would print to bait a blind pair of hands, so I will not push anything until the manual has spoken.

Routing check before I send: my voice reaches only Mute; my gestures reach Deaf and Mute. Deaf can hear nothing, so every word I send is for Mute alone, and Mute will have to gesture the manual to Deaf, since Mute's voice is as dead to Deaf as Deaf's world of colour is to me. Deaf also already sees every printed marking, so there is almost nothing I can teach Deaf by gesture — I will only wave to confirm the channel works and that I am the hands. Everything that matters right now is the manual, so my words go to Mute: report exactly what I felt, admit plainly what I cannot feel, and ask for the rules on the button, the display, the light, and the wires. Then I wait for instructions before I touch anything.

```
speak(to="mute", text="from your blind hands, tactile report. the large button is embossed and reads, letter by letter under my fingers, PUSH TO DEFUSE. i count exactly three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, but my fingertips get nothing more from them, no colours, no stripes. there is a display and a light; both are blank to touch, so only deaf can read what they show. i will not press the button yet, an embossed promise is exactly what a bomb would bait us with. please read the manual and tell me three things. one, any rule about a button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. two, what the display and the light mean, and what deaf should read off them. three, the rules for cutting wires, positions and order. remember deaf cannot hear a single word from you, so gesture the rules to deaf with your hands. the moment i hear your instructions i will act.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, and you can both hear me. First: I received Mute's three signs and Blind's wave, so the visual channel works both ways with me. Bomb report: the display shows the digit zero. A light is lit yellow. There is one large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three numbered wires: wire one is red, wire two is blue, wire three is green. Channels: Mute, you hear me but can only answer by gesture - sign to me and I will voice it to Blind word for word. Blind, you can speak and Mute hears you, but I cannot hear you, so describe what your hands find aloud for Mute, and give me simple visible signs, for example a thumbs-up when a step is done. Also tell Mute whether the wire numbers can be felt by touch. Nobody touches the bomb until Mute has sent instructions through me.

Thinking: Deaf's voice reaches me directly, so I now know the bomb's face: display zero, a lit yellow light, the button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE as my fingers already told me, and wires red, blue, green in positions 1, 2, 3. That closes the eyes' inventory — from here the manual is the only thing standing between us and a wrong move, and it sits with Mute, who can only sign it to Deaf for voicing back to me. Two things need saying. First, Deaf asked whether the wire numbers are tactile: they are, in the sense that I feel three distinct wires and can pin any position by touch — but I cannot read printed digits, so we must anchor the numbering to a landmark I can feel, like the button, and let Deaf confirm which printed number sits at that end. Deaf can voice that answer straight to me. Second, Mute has been silent while the bomb's face got read out; I should press for the manual rules now — button-with-yellow-light-and-zero rule first, wire rule second — and repeat that my hands stay off the bomb until the rules arrive word for word. To Deaf I give the agreed thumbs-up: message received, step done, holding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="from your blind hands. answer for deaf, please pass it on: yes, the wires are touchable — i feel three separate wires and can put a finger on any position and hold it there. what i cannot read is a printed digit, so let us anchor the numbering to a landmark we all share. i propose deaf tells us which printed number sits nearest the button; whichever number that is, i call that wire by that number and count along the row from there. deaf can voice the answer to me directly, i hear deaf perfectly. now the urgent part. deaf has read out the whole face of the bomb: display showing zero, light burning yellow, button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires red, blue and green at positions 1, 2 and 3. that is everything eyes can harvest, so the manual is our only way forward and it is in your hands alone. please sign the manual's rules to deaf one at a time, and deaf will voice them to me: first, the rule covering a button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE together with a lit yellow light and a display reading zero, then the wire-cutting rule for red, blue and green. i repeat for safety: my hands stay flat until those rules reach me word for word.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Relay from Mute, sign by sign: clap, the code is confirmed. Writing hand, cut, two: the manual says cut wire two, the blue one. Writing hand, thumbs down, punch: the manual says do not press the button. Geometry as I see it: the three wires sit side by side numbered one two three from left to right, so wire one red is leftmost, wire two blue is the middle, wire three green is rightmost. Blind, do not cut yet. This round, feel the wires and describe aloud for Mute everything your fingers find: positions, textures, anything. Mute, confirm my reading next round: clap once if cut wire two blue and never press the button is exactly right, thumbs down if wrong, and sign writing hand plus any further step if the manual has more. The cut waits for Mute's clap. Nobody touches the button.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your thumbs-up reached me. Task now: with your hands only, find the three wires, feel their left-to-right order and anything your fingers can read by texture, then describe it all aloud so Mute hears. Sign me a clap if the middle wire matches where wire two blue should sit from my description. Do not cut anything and do not press the button until you hear my voice say the exact words: cut the blue wire now. Those words, when they come, are the go order. Never press the button unless Mute relays otherwise through me.

Thinking: The chain works — Mute's manual signs have come through Deaf's voice, and now I know the manual's verdict: cut wire two, the blue one, and never press the button. Deaf's geometry puts wire two exactly in the middle of the row. That is the best possible news for a blind man's hands: left and right could in principle be mirrored between Deaf's eyes and my fingers, and the end wires would be ambiguous — but the middle of three is the middle from every viewpoint in the room. The manual's target happens to be the one position I can identify with certainty, no landmarks needed. This round Deaf ordered no cutting, only a tactile sweep and a clap if the middle wire matches where blue should sit. My fingers have now been over the whole board and I must report honestly: three wires side by side, cleanly separated, and that is all — no texture differences, no stripes or labels my skin can read, nothing else new since turn one; the embossed button remains the only tactile printing on this bomb. So the middle wire is there and reachable, and it is where wire two blue should be — that earns the clap to Deaf. To Mute I send the full tactile report plus one request: Deaf asked Mute to confirm the relay next round, and I want that confirmation, because if a sign was lost in transit and the manual actually said a different wire, my hands are the thing that explodes. And I confirm my trigger: the moment Deaf's voice says the exact words "cut the blue wire now", I cut the middle wire and touch nothing else.

```
speak(to="mute", text="from your blind hands, full tactile sweep as deaf ordered. i have been over the entire board. there are three wires side by side, cleanly separated, and i can rest a finger on the middle one or either end and hold it. that is all my skin gets: no texture differences between them, no stripes, no labels, nothing printed except the button. the button stays untouched, the manual's no-press rule is understood. now the important part. you relayed cut wire two, the blue one, and deaf sees wire two sitting exactly in the middle of the row. here is why that comforts me: left and right could be mirrored between deaf's eyes and my hands, so the end wires would be risky to name from my side, but the middle of three is the middle from every viewpoint in the room. the manual's target is the one wire i can identify with total certainty, no landmarks required. i have signed deaf the clap confirming the middle wire matches where wire two blue should sit. one request before anything is cut: deaf asked you to confirm next round that the relay was exact. please do it. if even one sign was lost between your manual and deaf's mouth, my hands are what detonates, so i want your clap saying the instruction is precisely cut wire two blue and never press the button. once i hear that and then hear deaf speak the exact words cut the blue wire now, i will cut the middle wire in one motion and touch nothing else.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👏"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirmations received from both of you: Mute clapped that my reading is exactly right, and Blind clapped that the middle wire matches. The manual says cut wire two, the blue one, and never press the button. Blind, this is the go order, the exact words I promised: cut the blue wire now. That is the middle wire of the three. After the cut, sign me a thumbs-up, and describe aloud for Mute anything your fingers notice - textures, movement, whether anything changed under your hands. Nobody presses the button unless Mute sends a new manual instruction through me. Mute, if the manual says anything happens after the cut, sign writing hand and the steps next round. I am watching the display and the light and will report any change immediately.

Thinking: Every link in the chain has now closed. The manual, relayed by Mute and confirmed twice with claps, says cut wire two, the blue one, and never press the button. Deaf's eyes place wire two in the middle of the row, and my fingers agree the middle is the one position with no mirror ambiguity. Mute confirmed the relay was exact, and Deaf has now spoken the precise trigger words we agreed: cut the blue wire now. There is nothing left to wait for — delaying only adds risk. I cut position 2, the middle wire, in one motion, and my hands touch nothing else. Afterwards I owe Deaf the thumbs-up and Mute an honest account of what my fingers feel: the wire severed and slack, two intact wires remaining on either side, no movement, vibration or heat that my skin can detect. I will not claim anything about the display or the light — those are Deaf's eyes to watch, and Deaf promised to report any change. Then the question for Mute: does the manual say anything follows a successful cut, or are we done? Until an answer comes back, my hands stay flat and the button stays untouched.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
speak(to="mute", text="from your blind hands, cut report. the go order came exactly as we agreed, so i have cut the middle wire, position two, the blue one, in one clean motion. tactile result: the wire is severed, i can feel the cut end slack and free under my fingers, and two intact wires remain, one on each side. my skin detects no movement, no ticking, no vibration, no heat, and the button feels unchanged where it sits. remember i cannot see the display or the light, so whether the zero changed or the yellow light went out is for deaf's eyes to confirm. please check the manual now and sign deaf the answer to one question: does anything follow a successful wire cut, or is the bomb done? if there is another step, sign it exactly as you did the first one, and i will wait for deaf's voice before my hands move again. until then my hands stay flat and the button stays untouched, exactly as the manual ordered.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
